newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares slide at open on Wall Street plunge.
newsitem.headline: French shares slide at open on Wall Street plunge.

text.p: French shares opened sharply lower on Friday on the back of Wall Street's 160-point dive sparked by fears of U.S. interest rate tightening.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index opened down 1.61 percent at 2,589.79 points before recovering slightly to trade 1.41 percent or 27.20 points lower at 2,594.72 at 1010 GMT.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down 1.22 percent or 32.0 points at 2,600.

The U.S. market's 2.3 percent fall was prompted by a bigger than expected gain in February retail sales which raised concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting council would raise interest rates at its next meeting on March 25.
Paris traders said the bourse was partly sustained by expectations that higher U.S. rates would push up the dollar.
One broker said the selling pressure was limited. "We've been falling for three days now," he said. He also said there was strong support at 2,595 points. "That seems to be holding."
But he said investors would trade cautiously ahead of U.S. producer price data due at 1330 GMT.
Volume was 1.1 billion francs in the first 30 minutes.

Shares in PSA Peugeot Citroen were unchanged at 642 francs after rising sharply on Thursday. Traders said investors expect the carmaker to announce restructuring measures after Renault's recent moves. "After Renault's experience, people expect Peugeot to do it more skillfully," a broker said.

Shares in Assurances Generales de France (AGF) fell 4.48 percent to 204.90 francs, the biggest fall in the CAC index, after the group expressed interest in bidding for state insurer GAN slated for privatisation.
